errors.english: suppose there were two men who were extremely fierce
errors.why: མི་གཉིས་པ means 'a second man' (contrasted with the first man of the preceding example), and the following མི་དེས refers to that one man, not 'one of two men'.

note: A faithful rendering of the Kāśyapaparivarta citation; only the 'second man' is misread as 'two men'.
Accurate rendering of the Abhidharma account of the intermediate eons and the three calamities.

errors.english: It would be better to enter a dwelling place filled with glowing embers than one line of text missing or cut off
errors.why: The verse continues on the next side ('...better than for a householder to spend the night in the Sangha's dwelling'); 'one line of text missing or cut off' is a stray artefact, not translation.

fix.find: glowing embers than one line of text missing or cut off

errors.english: (superior intention) the altruistic resolve of a bodhisattva
errors.why: ལྷག་པའི་བསམ་པ here is simply the nāga's earnest, wholehearted intention in taking refuge, not the bodhisattva's altruistic resolve.

note: Sound translation of the Sāgara episode and the verses on misuse of Sangha property, marred by a stray artefact at the end.
A difficult Pramāṇavārttika commentary on consecration and the 'heaviness' of sin, followed closely, with a few obscure but not wrong sentences.
Accurate rendering of the Vinaya commentary on proxy consent and a monk detained on the poṣadha day.

errors.english: the text states **furthermore**, and so on
errors.why: The lemma quoted as the reply is 'that too is untenable', not 'furthermore' (གཞན་ཡང་ comes only in the next sentence).

fix.find: the text states **furthermore**, and so on
fix.replace: the text states **that too is untenable**, and so on

note: Good commentary translation with one misquoted lemma, which hides the reply.

errors.english: the filaments of the light rays of her face
errors.why: The previous side ends ཁྱེད་ཀྱི་སོ་, so this is the prince's direct address: 'the filament-tips of the rays of YOUR TEETH', not 'her face'.

errors.english: she feigned sleep [note: original: (gnyid brdzun)], and I was occupied with gazing at her face. Then, out of modesty suitable for the occasion, she suddenly opened her eyes and laughed.
errors.why: Most likely he feigned sleep and she, absorbed in gazing at his face, grew abashed when he suddenly opened his eyes and laughed; the English reverses who sleeps, who gazes and who laughs.

note: The narrative prose is broadly right, but the ornate verses on the lovers confuse who does what to whom.
Faithful rendering of the argument on universals, particulars and recognition.

errors.why: དམ་བཅས་པ here is the convention or agreement (samaya) set up by the powerful persons who instituted the mantras (the next side glosses it as བརྡ), not a logical thesis.

fix.replace: If such a convention (samaya) remains in force

note: Accurate on the apauruṣeya debate, apart from one technical term in the closing mantra argument.

errors.english: That which is invisible but causes these practices is called Dharma
errors.why: In Vaiśeṣika, dharma is the unseen (adṛṣṭa) produced by these visible ritual practices; the practices are its cause, not its effect.

note: A careful rendering of the Vaiśeṣika doxography; the one slip inverts how the visible practices relate to the unseen force they produce.
